title: Upload results artifact format (JSON + parquet stub) with consistent metadata tags
author: Rina Kobayashi
release_notes: Benchmark-lab now uploads a versioned results artifact (results.json + results.parquet placeholder) with normalized metadata tags (gpu_sku, quant_mode, runtime_commit, workload_preset, etc.) for ingestion into dashboards/reporting.
description:
Motivation: As part of the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint, we need a defensible, repeatable results artifact that can be ingested by (1) the report generator and (2) quant-perf dashboards/alerts. Prior runs produced ad-hoc JSON with inconsistent tag keys (e.g., gpu vs gpu_type vs sku) and missing runtime provenance, making cross-run comparisons noisy and manual.

What this PR does: Implements a versioned results artifact format and an upload step that emits (a) results.json as the canonical human-readable artifact and (b) results.parquet as a stub/placeholder for the next iteration (schema stable, but currently only mirrors the JSON rows for easy adoption by downstream tooling). The artifact includes normalized metadata tags that are stable across GPUs/regions and are compatible with the planned dashboard dimensions.

Artifact layout (per run): - <run_dir>/results.json (required) - <run_dir>/results.parquet (optional, generated by default) - <run_dir>/manifest.txt (small, for quick inspection; includes artifact_version and upload URL)

Key fields (results.json): - artifact_version: "1.0" - created_at_utc: RFC3339 - run_id: stable UUID - tags: normalized string tags used for aggregation/filtering; includes: gpu_sku, gpu_count, gpu_mig, driver_version, cuda_version, runtime_repo, runtime_commit, runtime_version, container_digest, model_id, model_family, quant_mode (fp8|int8|fp16), fp8_format (e4m3|e5m2|n/a), scheduler_policy, workload_preset, request_shape (prefill_len/decode_len bins), streaming (true|false), region, bench_lab_pool (if set), and a freeform "notes" string. - metrics: flat key/value scalars for reporting (tokens_per_sec, ttft_ms_p50/p95, tpot_ms_p50/p95, prefill_ms_p50/p95, decode_ms_p50/p95, gpu_util_pct_avg where available) - samples: list of per-iteration summaries (kept intentionally small; full traces remain out-of-scope)

Parquet stub: results.parquet writes one row per (phase, metric) pair with columns: run_id, phase, metric, value, unit, plus tag columns duplicated for easy filtering. This is intentionally redundant to simplify ingestion by existing internal pipelines while the schema settles.

Normalization decisions: - gpu_sku is normalized to a stable token (A100-80GB, H100-SXM, H200-SXM, L40S) and we separately store raw_gpu_name from nvidia-smi for debugging. - quant_mode is strictly one of {fp16, fp8, int8}. FP8-specific parameters go under fp8_format and accumulation (added as tags, not nested config). - runtime_commit is required when running against a local runtime build; for hosted binary runs we populate runtime_version + build_id and set runtime_commit="unknown".

Uploader: Adds `benchctl upload-results` which uploads artifacts to the configured bucket/prefix and prints a stable URL. The uploader also writes a small manifest file locally with the upload destination and SHA256 of results.json to make reruns auditable.

Validation/backwards compatibility: - Adds JSON schema validation on write (and on upload). - Keeps the legacy `results_legacy.json` writer behind `--emit-legacy-results` for one sprint to avoid breaking any existing ad-hoc parsing scripts.

Testing: - Unit tests for tag normalization (gpu_sku parsing, quant_mode validation, required provenance fields). - Golden-file test for results.json output to catch accidental schema drift. - Integration test that runs a tiny synthetic benchmark and verifies upload packaging and schema validation.

Notes for reviewers: The list of tags is intentionally broader than what dashboards use today; the expectation is that we can ignore unused tags downstream. I tried to keep the schema flat to avoid nested/optional object churn. Follow-ups (not in this PR): (1) add per-op kernel IDs once PR #10621 lands in runtime tracing, and (2) wire this artifact into the report generator (ENG-24818) and dashboard ingestion.

Related: ENG-24818 (report generator), ENG-24810 (sprint umbrella).
commits: benchctl: add results artifact writer and schema validation
uploader: package run_dir artifacts and upload to bench-artifacts bucket
parquet: add results.parquet stub writer with stable columns
tests: golden output + normalization unit tests
docs: update benchmark run output docs and troubleshooting notes
conversation: Noah Patel (review): Love the direction. Two asks: (1) please make gpu_sku normalized and store raw name separately (we've had H100 variants bite us), and (2) can we guarantee runtime_commit is always present for perf-lab runs? Otherwise comparisons are suspect.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Updated normalization to emit gpu_sku from a small allowlist and store raw_gpu_name. For runtime_commit, I made it required when `--runtime-source=local` and added a validation error if missing. For packaged/binary runs, we set runtime_commit="unknown" and require runtime_version/build_id.

Allison Grant (review): For dashboards we need tags to be stable strings and avoid nested objects. Can we flatten fp8 settings into tags (fp8_format, accumulation) rather than an embedded config blob? Also would be great to include region + workload_preset explicitly.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Done. fp8_format and fp8_accumulation are now tags. Added required tags: region and workload_preset. Also added streaming=true|false as a tag since TTFT/TPOT dashboards will filter on it.

Sean Gallagher (review): Upload path: please make sure this doesn't spam large uploads by default in CI. Also can we include checksums in a manifest file for auditability? We've had partial uploads when nodes are contended.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Good call. CI uses `--upload=off` already, but I made uploader opt-in unless BENCHLAB_UPLOAD=1. Added manifest.txt with destination + SHA256 for results.json and list of files uploaded. Integration test uses dry-run upload.

Isabella Rossi (review): Minor naming: 'tokens_per_second' vs 'tokens_per_sec' is inconsistent with other scripts. Preference is tokens_per_sec. Also please keep the samples list small; full per-request arrays get huge fast.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Renamed to tokens_per_sec everywhere and added a guard that samples are capped (default 25) with a warning if truncated. Golden file updated.
Noah Patel (review): One more: can we add artifact_version at the top-level and lock it in a golden test so downstream consumers can branch safely? Then I'm good.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Added artifact_version="1.0" and a golden test asserting exact output keys. Thanks.
Allison Grant (approve): This will make ingestion way easier. Approving after the fp8 tag flattening changes.
Sean Gallagher (approve): Upload behavior + manifest look safe. Approving.
Noah Patel (approve): Looks solid and matches what we need for the sprint report tooling. Approving.
